mutations.because: An ad click destination must be an http: or https: URL so ad servers can wrap and track the click. Allowing arbitrary protocols admits javascript: and data: URIs, creating an XSS vector and breaking click tracking.
A click destination must be validated as a string before URL parsing. Without the string type check, non-string values like numbers or objects bypass validation and corrupt brief serialization.
The brief loading boundary must invoke validateClickDestination so invalid or relative URLs are rejected when briefs are parsed.
The use case validates clickDestination for programmatic callers bypassing boundary parsing (defense-in-depth). Removing this check allows an unvalidated destination to run through generation.
clickDestination must be registered in BRIEF_KEY_ORDER so that dumpBrief serializes it in its deterministic canonical position after output rather than as an arbitrary leftover key.
fromBrief must carry the brief's clickDestination into EditorState so that saving the brief does not silently delete the destination.
